chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the budn, how they are marked. He said: “They are marked while kneeling, by slitting the right side of their hump, and they are slaughtered while standing, from the right side.”

key_terms.الْبُدْنِ: sacrificial camels offered in pilgrimage rites
key_terms.بَارِكَةٌ: kneeling or sitting with the forelegs bent
key_terms.تُشْعَرُ: they are marked ritually by making an incision as a sign of sacrificial designation
key_terms.تُنْحَرُ: it is slaughtered by nahr, the prescribed method for camels

ai.seo_question: How should sacrificial camels be marked and slaughtered according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the ritual handling of sacrificial camels in hajj. It explains the manner of ishʿār and the proper position for nahr, indicating the prescribed practice transmitted from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2574 - Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about how camels are marked (Ish'ar).
Imam (as) said: "They are marked while sitting, by slitting the right side of their hump, and they are slaughtered while standing, from their right side."
